declarations.name: Causal.minkowski_chronallyHomotopicOn_segment
declarations.statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} {W : Opens (Minkowski n)}, Convex ℝ ↑W → ∀ {lam : ℝ → Minkowski n}, (minkowski n).ChronalCurveOn W lam 0 1 → (minkowski n).ChronallyHomotopicOn W lam fun s => lam 0 + s • (lam 1 - lam 0)
declarations.standing: W convex. Sbierski Thm 3.1 Step 2.1 (InexSchwarzschild2.tex:567) as printed, in the chronal reading: λ is homotopic to the straight segment from λ(0) to λ(1), Sbierski's length maximising geodesic (:569). W = ⊤ is Sbierski's M_Mink. λ(0) = 0 is not assumed.

declarations.name: Causal.minkowski_chronalHomotopyOn_convexCombination
declarations.statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} {W : Opens (Minkowski n)}, Convex ℝ ↑W → ∀ {γ₀ γ₁ : ℝ → Minkowski n}, (minkowski n).ChronalCurveOn W γ₀ 0 1 → (minkowski n).ChronalCurveOn W γ₁ 0 1 → γ₁ 0 = γ₀ 0 → γ₁ 1 = γ₀ 1 → (minkowski n).ChronalHomotopyOn W (fun t s => (1 - t) • γ₀ s + t • γ₁ s) γ₀ γ₁
declarations.standing: W convex; γ₀, γ₁ future chronal curves of W over [0, 1] with γ₁ 0 = γ₀ 0 and γ₁ 1 = γ₀ 1. The homotopy itself: (t, s) ↦ (1 − t)·γ₀ s + t·γ₁ s.

declarations.name: Causal.minkowski_chronalCurveOn_iff
declarations.statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} {W : Opens (Minkowski n)} {c : ℝ → Minkowski n} {a b : ℝ}, (minkowski n).ChronalCurveOn W c a b ↔ ContinuousOn c (Icc a b) ∧ MapsTo c (Icc a b) ↑W ∧ ∀ s ∈ Icc a b, ∀ s' ∈ Icc a b, s < s' → (minkowski n).lt ⊤ (c s) (c s')
declarations.standing: Every open W, every segment [a, b]. The subtle point of the target: ChronalCurveOn asks ≪_N in every small open N; in Minkowski space this is the global cone condition, met inside a ball around c t (convex, so ≪_ball is the restriction of ≪ by Causal.Flat.lt_iff_of_convex, Causal/Flat/Form.lean:308) through the continuity of c.

declarations.name: Causal.minkowski_chronalCurveOn_segment
declarations.statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} {W : Opens (Minkowski n)}, Convex ℝ ↑W → ∀ {p q : Minkowski n}, p ∈ W → q ∈ W → (minkowski n).lt ⊤ p q → (minkowski n).ChronalCurveOn W (fun s => p + s • (q - p)) 0 1
declarations.standing: W convex, p q ∈ W, p ≪ q at ⊤.

declarations.name: Causal.minkowski_lt_top_convexCombination
declarations.statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} {x₀ y₀ x₁ y₁ : Minkowski n}, (minkowski n).lt ⊤ x₀ y₀ → (minkowski n).lt ⊤ x₁ y₁ → ∀ {t : ℝ}, t ∈ Icc 0 1 → (minkowski n).lt ⊤ ((1 - t) • x₀ + t • x₁) ((1 - t) • y₀ + t • y₁)
declarations.standing: t ∈ [0, 1]. The convexity of the open future timelike cone, read on pairs of points.

declarations.name: Causal.minkowski_lt_top_segment
declarations.statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} {p q : Minkowski n}, (minkowski n).lt ⊤ p q → ∀ {s s' : ℝ}, s < s' → (minkowski n).lt ⊤ (p + s • (q - p)) (p + s' • (q - p))
declarations.standing: p ≪ q at ⊤, s < s'.

declarations.name: Causal.sbierskiPrintedHomotopy
declarations.statement: {n : ℕ} → (ℝ → Minkowski n) → ℝ → ℝ → Minkowski n

declarations.name: Causal.minkowski_not_chronalCurveOn_sbierskiPrinted_zero
declarations.statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} (lam : ℝ → Minkowski n), lam 0 = 0 → ∀ (W : Opens (Minkowski n)), ¬(minkowski n).ChronalCurveOn W (sbierskiPrintedHomotopy lam 0) 0 1
declarations.standing: λ(0) = 0 (Sbierski's normalisation, :573); any open W, any n. The slice is 0 on [0, 1/2], and a chronal curve of a chronological open set is injective (ChronalCurveOn.injOn, Causal/TimelikeHomotopy.lean:172).

findings: InexSchwarzschild2.tex:577–579 (Thm 3.1 Step 2.1). The printed homotopy Γ(t, s) = (σ_{λ(t)} * λ|[t,1])(s) is not a timelike homotopy. Its slice at t = 0 is σ_0 = 0 on [0, 1/2] (λ(0) = 0, :573). Its slice at t = 1 is λ|[1,1] = λ(1) on [1/2, 1]. A curve that pauses is not timelike under Sbierski's own Def 2.1 (:235): its derivative there is 0. It is not chronal either. This is now proved in Lean in ℝ^{1,n} for every n and every open set: Causal.minkowski_not_chronalCurveOn_sbierskiPrinted_zero, _one, minkowski_not_chronalHomotopyOn_sbierskiPrinted. Before, the Lean witness was on the timelike line only (Causal.timelikeLine_not_chronalCurveOn_pause). The defect does not depend on the rescaling of :579 (argued): at t = 1 the interval [1, 1] is a point, and at t = 0 σ_{λ(0)} = σ_0 is constant whatever the rescaling. The interior slices are chronal and Γ is jointly continuous (argued, not in Lean). The fault is only at the two ends.

The correction 'split at s = t' (binder row schwthm:MinkInex, `findings`) is proved: Causal.minkowski_chronalHomotopyOn_sbierskiSplit. Its form is Γ(t, s) = λ(0) + (s/t)(λ(t) − λ(0)) for s ≤ t and λ(s) for s ≥ t, a chronal homotopy with fixed endpoints from λ to the straight segment. It holds in every convex open set of ℝ^{1,n} and needs no normalisation λ(0) = 0. Its joint continuity at the corner (0, 0), the one delicate point, is Causal.continuousOn_sbierskiSplitHomotopy. The shorter route, the convex combination (1 − t)λ₀ + tλ₁, proves Step 2.1 (:567) and the remark of :835 directly. So the step itself stands; only the printed homotopy is defective.
questions: Timelike curves read as future chronal curves (Causal.TimelikeHomotopy's reading, kb/0273, not a new one). Under the C0 model the two classes are incomparable. For Sbierski's piecewise smooth timelike curves, route (a) also proves his form, because a convex combination of two piecewise smooth timelike curves is piecewise smooth and timelike (the future timelike cone is convex). That is argued, not in Lean: lean-causal has no smooth curves. Whether the binder row should say so is the keeper's or the author's choice.

'λ|[t,1] reparametrised to [0,1] (for example by a linear rescaling)' (:579). I took the linear rescaling u ↦ λ(t + u(1 − t)) to define the printed homotopy. The refutation does not depend on that choice (argued in findings), but the Lean statement is for the linear one.

Sbierski's normalisation 'without loss of generality λ(0) = 0' (:573). The positive results do not use it: the segment s ↦ λ(0) + s(λ(1) − λ(0)) and the split homotopy are translated forms. The refutation of the slice at t = 0 uses it, since the printed σ_X is written for it. Without it, the printed slice at t = 0 is the segment from the origin to λ(0), then λ, which is not even a curve from λ(0).

'The unique Lorentzian length maximising timelike geodesic' (:567, :569) I read as the straight segment, as :569 recalls. Its maximality is metric (T-loc-minkowski-timelike-diameter, DEC-147's package) and is not stated here.
kb_proposals: In Minkowski space the chronal curves of any open W over [a, b] are exactly the continuous maps into W with c s ≪ c s' at ⊤ for s < s' (Causal.minkowski_chronalCurveOn_iff). The local condition of ChronalCurveOn is met inside a ball, where ≪ restricts (Causal.Flat.lt_iff_of_convex). It is the Minkowski cousin of timelikeLine_chronalCurveOn_iff and the quick way to build chronal curves and homotopies of ℝ^{1,n} (T-loc-minkowski-future-one-connected).

Minkowski space is future one-connected on every convex open set by the convex combination (Causal.minkowski_futureOneConnectedOn). Sbierski's printed Step 2.1 homotopy is refuted in ℝ^{1,n} (minkowski_not_chronalHomotopyOn_sbierskiPrinted), and its split-at-s = t correction is proved (minkowski_chronalHomotopyOn_sbierskiSplit). Joint continuity at the corner (0, 0) comes from ‖(s/t)(λ t − λ 0)‖ ≤ ‖λ t − λ 0‖ on {0 ≤ s ≤ t}, glued to λ ∘ snd by ContinuousOn.union_of_isClosed.
